citations.narrative:
Throughout the facility there are multiple enclosures with broken floor wiring which are creating sharp end points within
the enclosure, the following enclosures were noted: 1 cage with 4 red cherry heads, 1 cage with 2 violet ringnecks, 1 cage
with 2 bluecrown conures, 1 cage with 1 mitrite conure, 1 bird in enclosure #643,1 cage with 1 ring neck, at least one bird
in cage number 255, at least one bird in cage number 247B,1 cage containing an approximately 50 year old macaw, and
one cage containing a one eyed macaw with broken wiring around the feeder.
In one enclosure containing 2 African grey parrots, the nest box has multiple sharp wire points sticking out into the entry
of the nest box.
In one enclosure containing 2 Cockatoos , there are sharp points coming out of the nest box and protruding into the
enclosure at the level of the birds.
One enclosure containing an approximately 50 year old macaw, has an approximately 8 inch strip of wire with sharp
points on the floor of the cage.
One enclosure with 2 capped parrots, has numerous wires with sharp ends hanging into the enclosure at the level of the
birds.
One enclosure, containing at least 3 birds, has a wooden perch held in place with a metal strip. The metal strip is broken
and has created sharp and jagged edges.
One enclosure with one Senegal has broken flooring and a broken rusted metal frame.
All of these broken metal wires and jagged edges may cause injury to the birds within the enclosures.
Housing facilities for birds must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound for the species of bird
housed in them. They must be kept in good repair, protect the birds from injury, and restrict other animals from entering
that may negatively affect the welfare of the birds within. The facility must repair, replace or alter all enclosures with the
broken metal and sharp points to protect the birds from injury.
Correction Date : December 22, 2026.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
One blue crown conure has bilateral eye abnormalities. Both eyes are fully opaque with mild occasional squinting.
Licensee had not noticed the condition of the bird's eyes. Failure to notice animal abnormities can worsen conditions at
hand, which may cause negative impacts on the health of the animals.
The dealer shall conduct daily observation of all animals to assess their health and well-being, There must be a
mechanism of direct and frequent communication is required so that timely and accurate information on problems of
animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian. The blue crown conure must be
evaluated by a licensed veterinarian for an accurate diagnosis and treatment plan.
To be corrected : the blue crown conure must be evaluated by the licensed veterinarian by Oct 29, 2026.
Beginning Oct 22,2026 : The facility must ensure daily observations are done in order to ensure daily animal health and
well being.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
